record.paper_title: Survey of solved and open problems in the degeneracy phenomenon
record.context_brief: Decision procedure for detecting simplex cycling from c ∈ M(C)
record.original_question: Given linear-program data (A, b, c) and a degenerate vertex x⁰, let G⁰ be the degeneracy graph at x⁰ and, for each circuit C of G⁰, let M(C) be the point set induced by (A, b, c) such that C is a simplex cycle exactly when c belongs to M(C). Can one design an efficient method that decides whether c ∈ M(C) for at least one circuit C of G⁰, and hence determines whether simplex cycling occurs?

evidence.quote: We are currently trying to develop a method which solves the problem: given (A, b, c) and a degenerate vertex x °, determine whether c ∈ M(C) for at least one C of G °. If so, simplex-cycling occurs.
We are at the very beginning of finding an efficient method to solve this problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a linear program in standard form
  minimize cᵀx subject to Ax = b, x ≥ 0,
where A is an m×n real matrix of rank m, b ∈ ℝᵐ, and c ∈ ℝⁿ. Let x⁰ be a degenerate basic feasible solution (vertex), i.e. a vertex represented by more than one feasible basis. The degeneracy graph G⁰ at x⁰ is the undirected graph whose vertices are all feasible bases representing x⁰, with two such bases joined by an edge whenever they differ by exactly one basis-exchange (a single simplex pivot).

A circuit C of G⁰ is a simple cycle B₁ – B₂ – … – B_k – B₁ in this graph. For fixed (A, b) and a fixed circuit C of G⁰, define
  M(C) = { c ∈ ℝⁿ : when the simplex method is applied with cost vector c, it can perform exactly the pivot sequence around C, returning to B₁ },
so that the simplex method cycles along C precisely when c ∈ M(C). Simplex cycling occurs at x⁰ for the data (A, b, c) if and only if c ∈ M(C) for some circuit C of G⁰.

Problem. Design an algorithm that, given (A, b, c) and a degenerate vertex x⁰, decides in time polynomial in the input size (or otherwise efficiently) whether there exists a circuit C of G⁰ with c ∈ M(C); equivalently, decides whether simplex cycling can occur at x⁰ for the data (A, b, c).
artifact.category_tag: Linear programming degeneracy and simplex cycling
artifact.status_search_result: A web search on degeneracy graphs and simplex cycling returns the survey on degeneracy graph theory and related expositions, but no source confirming an efficient algorithm to decide membership c ∈ M(C) for some circuit C of the degeneracy graph. The status of an efficient decision procedure for cycling detection via the M(C) framework appears unresolved in the accessible literature.

status_evidence.title: Degeneracy graphs: theory and application — an updated survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey covering basic properties of degeneracy graphs, cycling of the simplex method, the neighborhood problem and applications.
status_evidence.claim: The updated survey discusses cycling via degeneracy graphs but does not announce an efficient decision procedure for c ∈ M(C).

status_evidence.title: Degeneracy problems in mathematical programming and degeneracy graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses degeneracy phenomena and degeneracy graphs in LP.
status_evidence.claim: No efficient algorithm for testing c ∈ M(C) over circuits of G⁰ is presented.
